editorial.tldr: On Oct 31 DeepSeek's harness team put the architecture of dsh-superagent, an always-on router-worker coding agent, on GitHub as a research prototype. Press coverage from Nov 1 to Nov 4 framed it as a challenge to Claude Code that watches team chat for work and fixes bugs on its own.
editorial.whats_new: Former DeepSeek core member Zhang Bo open-sourced a separate personal agent on Nov 20 that reportedly runs a 125B model locally on a 12GB GPU; it is not a DeepSeek release.
editorial.why_it_matters: dsh-superagent is a published reference design for a proactive, chat-triggered coding agent from a frontier lab, but it ships as a research prototype and every capability claim so far comes from press rewrites, not hands-on evaluation.
editorial.take_for_builders: Read the dsh-superagent repo as a design reference for chat-triggered agents, but do not deploy it until a license and an independent evaluation exist.

open_questions: Will anyone publish a hands-on evaluation of dsh-superagent on real repositories?
What license does dsh-superagent ship under, and which models can its router and workers use?
Will DeepSeek move dsh-superagent beyond a research prototype into a maintained product?
Does the 125B-on-12GB claim for Zhang Bo's agent hold up, and at what quantization and speed?
